title: Smallest equivalent DNF
description: Formulas in disjunctive normal form with at most k terms that are equivalent to a given one (here: not all of x1..xn are equal); existence is Sigma-2-complete (Umans). The abstraction picks terms from a pool, the check finds an assignment on which the two formulas differ, and the refinement depends on that assignment alone: use a term that covers it, or drop the terms that cover it. Try n = 4, k = 4 (6 solutions among more than a million candidates).

fragments.name: shared
fragments.description: The given formula and the pool of terms. Added to every solver.
fragments.text:
% Variables x1..xn.
var(1..n).
% The given formula is the disjunction of the n(n-1) terms  x_I & ~x_J  (I != J).
% It is true unless all variables have the same value.
given(I,J) :- var(I), var(J), I != J.
% The pool: every non-empty conjunction of literals may be a term of the answer.
% Term number P is read in base 3: digit V says whether x_V is absent (0), plain (1)
% or negated (2). has(P,V,S): term P contains x_V with sign S.
pool(1..3**n-1).
has(P,V,S) :- pool(P), var(V), S = (P / 3**(V-1)) \ 3, S > 0.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k terms from the pool.
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k terms from the pool.
{ use(P) : pool(P) } k.
% Shown as term(P,V) for the literal x_V and term(P,-V) for its negation.
#show.
#show term(P,V)  : use(P), has(P,V,1).
#show term(P,-V) : use(P), has(P,V,2).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.description: The interface atoms: which terms of the pool are used.

fragments.name: check
fragments.description: Looks for an assignment on which candidate and given formula differ (solver C); states the refinement as clause/3 atoms.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an assignment a/1 to the variables ...
{ a(V) } :- var(V).
% ... on which the candidate and the given formula differ.
% covers(P): term P of the pool is true under the assignment.
off(P) :- has(P,V,1), not a(V).
off(P) :- has(P,V,2), a(V).
covers(P) :- pool(P), not off(P).
mine :- use(P), covers(P).
theirs :- given(I,J), a(I), not a(J).
:- mine, theirs.
:- not mine, not theirs.
#show a/1.

% The assignment tells every later candidate what to do, whatever its other terms are.
% The given formula is true here: use one of the terms that cover the assignment.
clause(0, use(P), true) :- theirs, covers(P).
% The given formula is false here: each used term that covers the assignment has to go.
clause(P, use(P), false) :- not theirs, use(P), covers(P).

fragments.name: check_relevant
fragments.description: Variant relevant: the same check with relevant/1 (one covering term must flip) instead of clause/3.
fragments.text:
% A counterexample: an assignment a/1 to the variables ...
{ a(V) } :- var(V).
% ... on which the candidate and the given formula differ.
% covers(P): term P of the pool is true under the assignment.
off(P) :- has(P,V,1), not a(V).
off(P) :- has(P,V,2), a(V).
covers(P) :- pool(P), not off(P).
mine :- use(P), covers(P).
theirs :- given(I,J), a(I), not a(J).
:- mine, theirs.
:- not mine, not theirs.
#show a/1.

% The assignment refutes the candidate as long as no term that covers it changes: one of them
% must flip (be used if the given formula is true here, go if it is false). Weaker than the
% clauses of the check fragment, which ask for every wrong term to go.
relevant(use(P)) :- covers(P).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The refinement depends on the counterexample only, so the check writes it down
# itself as clause(Id, Atom, Value) atoms: one clause "use a covering term", or a unit
# clause for every wrong term. G.clauses(X) reads them.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clauses(X)

instances.facts: % The given formula on 3 variables, answers with at most 3 terms: 2 solutions.
% 2 variables (x1 xor x2), at most 2 terms: 1 solution.
% 3 variables, at most 2 terms: none (the formula needs 3 terms).
% 4 variables, at most 3 terms: none (the formula needs 4); the pool has 80 terms.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.block(M)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# The refinement from relevant/1: one of the terms that cover the assignment must flip.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X: reject M with G.clause(M, X)

solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

# Up to three counterexample assignments per candidate, the clauses of each.
search A:
    on candidate M:
        for X in C.models(assume G(M), limit 3):
            reject M with G.clauses(X)

spaces.description: Boolean functions on n = 1, 2, ... variables, at most k terms.
